title: One partition with pivot 2
summary: Move the right pointer j first and the left pointer i second. Swap misplaced elements, then place pivot 2 at the partition boundary.
context: Initially nums = [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5], indexed from 0 to 5. The current bounds are left = 0 and right = 5. The leftmost value nums[left] = 2 is the pivot.

From the left, i searches for the first element greater than the pivot. From the right, j searches for the first element smaller than the pivot. Each iteration moves j first, then i; both scans require i < j. Swap misplaced elements across the partition until the pointers meet. Finally swap the pivot into the meeting position.
description: The upper part shows nums, the pivot marker, the bounds left and right, and the scanning pointers i and j. Below it, gray highlighting marks the current statement of partition. Pivot 2 stays at index 0 throughout the scan, even as i moves. Only the final swap moves the pivot. The bounds stay left = 0 and right = 5 throughout; their labels are hidden in the final state.
result: One partition fixes the pivot’s final position. The subarrays on either side still need recursive sorting.

frames.title: Initialize the bounds, pivot, and two pointers
frames.explanation: Initially nums = [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5]. Choose 2 at index 0 as the pivot. The gray line i, j = left, right sets i = 0 and j = 5, pointing to 2 and 5 respectively. No scans or swaps yet.
frames.key_state: nums = [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5]; i = 0, j = 5; pivot 2 at index 0.
frames.announcement: Initialize i = 0 and j = 5. Choose the leftmost element 2 as pivot.

frames.title: Scanning from the right, j finds 0 below the pivot
frames.explanation: Move j first. Skip 5 at index 5 and 3 at index 4: neither is smaller than pivot 2. At index 3, 0 < 2, so stop. Now nums = [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5], i = 0, j = 3; pivot 2 remains at index 0.
frames.key_state: nums = [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5]; i = 0, j = 3; pivot 2 at index 0. j stopped at 0, smaller than pivot 2.
frames.announcement: j moves left past 5 and 3 and stops at 0 at index 3.

frames.title: Scanning from the left, i finds 4 above the pivot
frames.explanation: Next move i. At index 0, 2 is no greater than pivot 2, so pass it. At index 1, 4 > 2, so stop. Now nums = [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5], i = 1 points to 4 and j = 3 to 0. These elements are ready to swap. Pivot 2 is still at index 0.
frames.key_state: nums = [2, 4, 1, 0, 3, 5]; i = 1, j = 3; pivot 2 at index 0. i stopped at 4, greater than pivot 2. The swap is next.
frames.announcement: i stops at 4 at index 1, ready to swap it with 0 at j.

frames.title: Swap 4 and 0
frames.explanation: Swap 4 at index 1 with 0 at index 3. The smaller value 0 moves left and the larger value 4 moves right. Now nums = [2, 0, 1, 4, 3, 5], i = 1, j = 3; pivot 2 remains at index 0.
frames.key_state: nums = [2, 0, 1, 4, 3, 5]; i = 1, j = 3; pivot 2 at index 0. The swap at indices 1 and 3 is complete.
frames.announcement: Swap 4 at index 1 with 0 at index 3.

frames.title: Continuing left, j finds 1 below the pivot
frames.explanation: In the next iteration j moves first. At index 3, 4 ≥ 2. Move left to index 2 and stop at 1 < 2. Now nums = [2, 0, 1, 4, 3, 5], i = 1 points to 0, j = 2 points to 1; pivot 2 remains at index 0.
frames.key_state: nums = [2, 0, 1, 4, 3, 5]; i = 1, j = 2; pivot 2 at index 0. j stopped at 1, smaller than pivot 2.
frames.announcement: j moves left from 4 to 1 at index 2.

frames.title: Pointer i moves right and meets j
frames.explanation: At index 1, 0 ≤ 2. Move i right to index 2, where it meets j. Now nums = [2, 0, 1, 4, 3, 5], i = j = 2. The meeting position holds 1 and pivot 2 remains at index 0. The inner scan for i stops because i < j is now false. No element greater than the pivot was found.
frames.key_state: nums = [2, 0, 1, 4, 3, 5]; i = 2, j = 2; pivot 2 at index 0. The pointers have met; the self-swap is still to come.
frames.announcement: i moves right to meet j at index 2. Scanning stops.

frames.title: Swapping the meeting position with itself leaves the array unchanged
frames.explanation: Run the nums[i], nums[j] swap at the end of this iteration. Since i = j = 2, the 1 at index 2 swaps with itself. Now nums is still [2, 0, 1, 4, 3, 5] and pivot 2 is still at index 0. The outer partition loop exits because i < j is false.
frames.key_state: nums = [2, 0, 1, 4, 3, 5]; i = 2, j = 2; pivot 2 at index 0. The self-swap left the array unchanged. The outer loop has ended.
frames.announcement: Both pointers are at the same position. Swapping there changes nothing, and the outer partition loop ends.

frames.title: Swap pivot 2 into boundary index 2
frames.explanation: After the loop, swap pivot 2 at index 0 with 1 at index 2. Now nums = [1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 5], i = j = 2. Pivot 2 has reached its final index 2.
frames.key_state: nums = [1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 5]; i = 2, j = 2; pivot 2 at index 2.
frames.announcement: Swap pivot 2 at index 0 with 1 at the meeting index 2. The pivot is in place.

frames.title: Finish the partition and leave the two subarrays for recursion
frames.explanation: Execute return i to return index 2. Now nums = [1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 5]. The labels left, right, i, j are hidden. Braces mark the left subarray [1, 0] (indices 0 through 1) and the right subarray [4, 3, 5] (indices 3 through 5). All elements on the left are ≤ 2 and all on the right are ≥ 2. Neither side is sorted internally yet.
frames.key_state: Return index 2. Now nums = [1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 5]. The left subarray [1, 0] and right subarray [4, 3, 5] await recursive sorting. The pointer labels are hidden.
frames.announcement: Partition complete. Index 2 is returned. Both subarrays still require recursive sorting.
